images.title: One million: cellular neighborhoods
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Primary request: a beautiful, spacious, high-fidelity Board map interface exploring very large process populations with an organic fabric. Landscape, wide 16:9 desktop composition.
The attached image is a MATERIAL AND SEMANTIC REFERENCE ONLY. Keep its warm ivory fabric, dark teal text and restrained amber age coloration, and the idea that a broad positive shoulder represents an inbox while a narrower depression from that shoulder represents an outbox. REPLACE its crowded UI and repetitive little volcano grid with the new composition below.
UI composition: almost edge-to-edge canvas occupying over ninety percent of the screen below one slim 56px header. No left navigation rail. No permanent right sidebar. No large title block. No repeated group totals, secondary overview diagram, mini-map, ranked list, cross-section chart, or instructional paragraphs. Use whitespace inside the map; all controls are compact and generously separated. A small Board wordmark and the specified scope breadcrumb on the left of the single header, a single search field "Search processes or groups" in the center, and a small "Map / Browse" toggle on the right. Map is selected.
Under the header at upper left show the specified population once in medium 22px type, not a gigantic dashboard heading. The material surface occupies the rest of the width with a calm margin and room for its relief to breathe.
One single compact floating legend at bottom left: "Group totals · Inbox ↑  Outbox ↓", followed by a very small grey-to-amber strip labeled "Oldest output  0 — 30m+". There is no second layer selector; the legend itself has one subtle chevron. At bottom right put one small control cluster with minus, plus, reset-view icon, and an "Evidence" button. Tiny footer "Concept · synthetic data".
Visual language: high-end cartographic/architectural clay relief. Near top-down view with a mild tilt just sufficient to see the shoulders and basin walls. Rounded stable group boundaries and fine sparse contour lines, with a continuous quiet neutral fabric between groups. Shapes should feel cellular through their irregular rounded boundaries, without literal biology or translucent jelly. Preserve positive shoulder and negative inset well as separate deformations; some groups have only a shoulder, some only a basin and a few are neutral. Amber is on the well walls only, with most surfaces grey-ivory. Do not tint all terrain amber. No connecting graph lines or process-level dots at these aggregate scales.
Use few labels, comfortable typography and strong hierarchy. White-space is part of the design, not an empty sidebar. The abstract groups are synthetic summaries, not thousands of individual process meshes or exact plots. Keep every requested word and number readable. Do not add other statistics, warning icons, brand logos or decorative biological details.

Header scope: "Atlas / A.01.01". Population: "1,000,000 processes".
Depict roughly forty distinct irregular softly polygonal group cells covering the broad canvas in a coherent connected fabric. Each is a small sculpted neighborhood rather than an isolated pin: broad raised rim/shoulder and a narrower scooped outbox depression with subtle amber inner-wall tone. Vary footprints and amplitudes. The groups are individually discernible, with only a few tiny contour steps each, substantially less repetitive than the reference. Quiet flat areas and open neutral seams give the cells breathing room.
Label only three representative group cells with small text "01", "14", "28". The first cell in the upper-left quarter contains the old-output outlier; one tiny outlined flag "47m" anchors to that containing cell. No PID number, no inspector, no extra badges or lists. No artificial large outer hexagon. Preserve the reference's fabric identity while making the overall interface much calmer and wider.

refinements.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine only the fabric geometry in this Board one-million-process mockup. Preserve every UI element, exact text, numeric label, population, group boundary, age flag position, palette and full-width composition.
Within a group that has both inbox and outbox work, the outbox hole must be scooped INTO THE CENTER OF THE SAME BROAD RAISED INBOX SHOULDER, like a shallow hollow crown. Currently several cells show a separate mound beside an unrelated pit; replace those detached pairs with a single organically shaped shoulder containing its own central depression. Keep group footprints irregular, vary counts through shoulder height and well depth, and keep fine sparse contours. A few cells may remain inbox-only mounds or outbox-only depressions. The selected 47m group's amber well must sit inside its raised shoulder. Do not introduce process dots, other controls, sidebars, extra labels or a regular volcano grid. Keep the spacious UI exactly as it is.

images.title: Billion-process overview with contextual inspection
images.prompt:
Edit this Board one-billion-process overview to show a single selected old-output result with a compact contextual card. Preserve the full-width fabric, camera, all group geometry, population text, header, bottom legend, zoom controls and Evidence button. Do not add a sidebar, mini-map, rail, extra chart or duplicated statistics.
Selection: delicately outline the existing upper-left Group A boundary in dark teal. Keep its A label. REMOVE the existing 47m flag, flag stem and orange anchor dot completely; the detail card now owns that age value. Do not draw an exact process point at this aggregate scale.
Place a small elegant floating card, approximately 330px wide by 245px tall at the top right of the map below the header, with generous internal spacing, warm white background and very subtle shadow. This overlays the map temporarily and is not a reserved column or full-height panel. Exact card text in clean readable sans-serif:
"PID 41773" as heading with small close X at top right.
"Within A · oldest output" as small secondary line.
"Inbox  0" and "Outbox  1" in one simple two-column row.
"Oldest pending  47m" on one row below.
One full-width modest dark teal button "Go to process".
No other card text. Do not repeat PID, queue counts, or 47m anywhere else on the page. Search stays empty. This is an on-demand evidence summary for a member within Group A, not the group total. Show no extra connectors between the card and group. Keep the interface airy, precise and calm.
